chapter: CCC camp, field work and gambling
title: The CCC camp in 1937
summary: He spent six months in the Civilian Conservation Corps doing land work, paid fifty dollars a month, and entertained on a piano the officer found for him.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: 35, well, I remember then I was beginning to start wanting to play music. And then broke in, around 37 I went to the CC camp. CC camp, what was that? Yeah, I came, well that's how, it's three C's, that's how we go, Algecultras. Oh, I can't pronounce the name right off hand. But take, at the time, what was it going to call it? The CCC camp, three C's. And maybe later on you'll find out where it represented. Probably Civil Construction Corps, Civil Corps.

Cooperation, yeah. What, you were working? So was it... Oh, that's what the idea was. What did you do? Did everything. We were planting trees, digging spillweeds, we were grading, we were sloping, we were building banks, we was cutting soil, we were laying soils. Yeah. We were opening up spillweeds, grading roads, putting gravel down, cutting trees if necessary. Yeah. Cleaning all the land.

Was this outside the city? Was this outside New Orleans? Yeah, just around Sweetport, all around Hardin. With all these people you worked, did you ever travel a great deal or did you just mostly stay around New Orleans?
Well, at CCC camp there was a lot of traveling in it.
You know what I mean? You never know where you're going until you get there. It's like a road crew. How did those things pay?
Did they, a dollar a day? What were they? Well, at that time I was getting fifty dollars a month. Oh yeah.

But if you had a dependent, well then they would send you a dependent fifty dollars a month and they would give you twenty-two, maybe twenty-eight, over there, where you was, where you were serving your time. And out of that you'd have to pay your laundry bills and, well you buy a canteen book, it's like you would spend checks and things out here, you bought canteen books in there and it represented money you know. So some guys I mean had other hustles in there besides that, which I did.
Did you play music while you were up to entertain the people?

Well the guy that was in charge of the company found out that I could play, and he got a piano from somewhere and put it in a recreation hall for me to entertain the soldiers so they would, you know, have something to do and somewhere to go. Well we'd knock off. Well I guess so I didn't have to drill much no more. Oh so this was, you were in the army? You were in the army?
Well you can consider it the army.
Oh I thought it was some type of civilian work thing. Well this was all through, it was under the army.
It was under the army. Rules, regulations, yeah. So you were. We sold it, yeah, we drilled, we did everything a soldier would do, all the things, we had working periods too, you know.
So this was all through the late 30s? This was in 37. Till how long did this last?
Well I stayed in there six months. Oh so this was? My time was up. Seemed like six years.
Really, with that work going on I wasn't expecting that. And you had to study, you had to go to school, you had to drill, and a whole lot of shit going on.
